# Injected message fixtures

How the messages the hub sends to the model in the user's name (task notifications, scheduled tasks, wake-ups, node restarts) are recognized, and what is recognized from them: the rules are in `docs/protocol/protocol.md`, "Messages injected by Persona".

| File | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `cases.json` | Every state of every template, a title with brackets, a snapshot block in front, and similar text the user typed (not recognized) |

- Structure: `{"version": 1, "cases": [...]}`. `input.text` is the user line in the transcript; `expected` is the `injected` the hub sends (`null` means not recognized, so it stays a user bubble). `todo_id` can only be added by the hub and is absent from the fixture.
- The cases are generated by a Go test from the rendered templates; after a template changes, regenerate them: `cd server && UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./internal/prompts -run Injected`.
- The web app's fallback recognition (`lib/injected.ts`), for a hub that sends no `injected` field, runs the same file. A missing field equals an empty one in the comparison.
